Dallas , Global
General Business , Mergers & Acquisitions , Internet / Technology
Texas Pacific Land to Acquire EagleRock in $3 Billion All-Stock Transaction
November 23, 2026
Texas Pacific Land Corporation (NYSE: TPL) has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire EagleRock Land, LLC (NYSE: EROK) in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $3 billion , expanding its land ownership, water infrastructure and royalty operations across the Permian Basin.
The transaction will combine two land and water management businesses with complementary holdings in the Midland and Delaware basins. The combined company is expected to own approximately 1 million fee surface acres, along with an additional 105,000 acres covered by water-related dedication agreements.
Under the merger agreement, EagleRock shareholders will receive 0.0831 shares of a newly formed holding company for each EagleRock Class A share. Based on Texas Pacific Land’s five-day volume-weighted average share price as of November 20, 2026, the exchange ratio represents approximately $23.56 per EagleRock share.
Holders of units in EagleRock Land Operating, LLC will receive shares at the same exchange ratio, with their paired EagleRock Class B shares canceled.
Existing Texas Pacific Land shareholders are expected to own approximately 86% of the combined company, while former EagleRock shareholders and operating company unitholders will hold approximately 14% on a fully diluted basis.
The transaction will involve a holding company reorganization under which New Titan Holdings, Inc. will become the publicly traded parent of both businesses. The holding company is expected to adopt the Texas Pacific Land Corporation name upon closing. Each existing TPL share will convert into one share of the new holding company.
The combined business will retain Texas Pacific Land’s board of directors and executive management team, with headquarters in Dallas.
EagleRock owns or controls approximately 288,000 acres across the Permian Basin, including roughly 59,000 fee-owned acres primarily in Lea County, New Mexico. The acquisition will expand Texas Pacific Land’s presence in the Delaware Basin and increase its Midland Basin surface acreage by nearly 40%.
EagleRock’s Midland Basin assets include approximately 220,000 barrels per day of produced water handling capacity through gathering, disposal and recycling infrastructure, along with approximately 130,000 barrels per day of non-potable water supply capacity.
Following the acquisition, Texas Pacific Land expects its combined water infrastructure platform to have approximately 1.5 million barrels per day of aggregate non-potable water sourcing and produced water treatment capacity, representing a 49% increase.
Combined water storage capacity is projected to reach approximately 68 million barrels, an increase of 79%.
The expanded acreage also includes approximately 37,600 future undrilled well locations within five miles of the combined properties, providing potential demand for water services, surface access and related infrastructure.
Texas Pacific Land expects the transaction to be accretive to estimated 2027 free cash flow per share before synergies.
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the combined businesses generated pro forma adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 83% and free cash flow margins of approximately 60%.

Sierra Raises $1.75B in Series F Funding at $30B Valuation
Published

By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent

Key Points Sierra's outcome-based pricing ties revenue to delivered results but makes margins…

Sierra's outcome-based pricing ties revenue to delivered results but makes margins sensitive to execution failures.
Ghostwriter lets teams define goals and guardrails while the system builds tests and deploys agents.
Sierra's constellation-of-models architecture routes tasks across 15 or more models to optimize latency and quality.
Sierra announced on November 23, 2026 that it is raising $1.75 billion in Series F funding at a $30 billion valuation, in a round led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company builds AI agents that handle customer interactions and carry out business tasks for large enterprises.
The terms follow Sierra’s May 4, 2026 announcement that it was raising $950 million, led by Tiger Global and GV, at a valuation above $15 billion. Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV and Tiger Global are participating again after previously serving as lead investors.
Enterprise Growth Behind the Round
Sierra reported on October 30, 2026 that annual recurring revenue (ARR) had passed $400 million, including more than $150 million added in the third quarter. That quarterly addition exceeded the ARR it added during the entire prior year.
The company said ARR took six months to double from $100 million to $200 million, then five months to double from $200 million to $400 million.
Customer adoption has accompanied that growth. Sierra reported working with more than 40% of the Fortune 50 in May and almost 50% by the October update. The latter disclosure also described a large US retailer with more than $40 billion in revenue going from its first meeting with Sierra to a live agent in 27 days.
The May announcement supplied further deployment measures: Nordstrom launched its Nora voice agent in five weeks; Singtel launched in 10 weeks with resolution rates above 70%; and Cigna entered production in eight weeks while reducing patient-authentication time by 80%.
Outcome Pricing and Its Constraints
Sierra’s outcome-based pricing charges for results such as a resolved problem, originated loan, paid insurance claim or retained subscriber, rather than basing its core model on seats, tokens or usage. The company says this aligns its incentives with customers’ business results, while making attrition and margin more directly sensitive when promised results are not delivered.
Sierra also describes the approach as more complex operationally, contractually and for accounting than seat- or consumption-based pricing. It works only when software is highly autonomous and the outcome can be cleanly attributed to it; Sierra retains consumption-style pricing where that better fits the problem.
Ghostwriter and the Model Architecture
Ghostwriter sits above that pricing model. Sierra says teams define goals and guardrails, and the system builds, tests and deploys agents. A September 28, 2026 update made Ghostwriter proactive inside Slack and Teams: it can review customer conversations, recommend changes and experiments, monitor results and identify when those results are statistically significant.

articles.title: India Digest: Tanglin backs Matters.AI; Ionic Wealth raises funding from parent
articles.snippet: India Digest: Tanglin backs Matters.AI; Ionic Wealth raises funding from parent DealStreetAsia
articles.text:
Matters.AI has raised about Rs 115 crore ($12 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, while Ionic Wealth has secured strategic funding from its parent company and a group of family offices.
Tanglin backs Matters.AI
Matters.AI, which is building an AI security engineer for data, has raised about Rs 115 crore ($12 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, per an announcement.
IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures and Tetration Ventures also participated, alongside existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners.
The latest round takes the company’s total funding to about Rs 175 crore ($18.25 million).
AI agents now read, copy and move enterprise data with the permissions of the employees who run them. Most data security tools show where sensitive data sits. They do not show who or what is using it, or why, so security teams connect alerts from separate tools by hand before they can respond.
“Security teams don’t need another tool telling them something might be wrong. They need a system that understands the problem, investigates it, and takes action,” said Keshava Murthy, Co-Founder and CEO of Matters.AI, in a statement.
Ionic Wealth raises funding from parent
Ionic Wealth, the wealth management platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in strategic funding from its parent company and a group of family offices.
The fundraise takes the platform’s total funding to Rs 466 crore, Angel One said in a media statement.
Ionic Wealth claims to have crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with a combined high-net-worth individual (HNI) and ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) client base of more than 2,900 across over 12 cities. The platform has a team of more than 100 private bankers and has achieved this scale within two years of operations.
The company plans to use the funding to strengthen its portfolio-led offerings and global capabilities, integrate AI into its wealth-tech platform, scale its UHNI business and expand its presence in India and overseas.
“This strategic investment validates our vision of building a new-age wealth platform at the intersection of domain expertise and technology,” said Srikanth Subramanian, Co-founder and CEO of Ionic Wealth, in a media statement.

Top Tech News: Nano Core Raises USD 1 Billion, Akash Launches GPU Marketplace
Chinese AI chip startup Nano Core has secured over RMB 1 billion in fresh funding, while Akash has introduced a new marketplace for future GPU computing capacity.
Written By : Akshita Pidiha
Reviewed By : Vijay Laxmi
Published: 23rd Nov, 2026 at 12:06 PM
Updated: 23rd Nov, 2026 at 12:06 PM
Good morning, tech fam! Here are some quick technology updates to keep you informed about the latest developments.
What’s New Today: Chinese AI chip startup Nano Core has raised over RMB 1 billion in Series C2 funding, highlighting growing investment in AI chip development.
Fast-Track Insights: Akash has launched a GPU computing marketplace that allows AI companies to secure future computing capacity at fixed prices. The platform supports Nvidia B300, H200 and RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell systems.
Here’s a quick rundown of today's biggest technology headlines. Let's explore the latest developments in AI chips, tech funding, graduate hiring, artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency.
Akash Launches Marketplace for Future GPU Computing Capacity
Akash has launched Akash Forwards, a marketplace where AI firms can reserve their GPU computing power for future months at fixed prices. The service uses daily bidding and US Dollar settlement. It includes Nvidia B300, H200, and RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell. A trial version is due in Q1 2027, while a general public release will happen in Q2 2027.

The firm expects to launch the fund between March and June 2027.
